description.text: The promos of Japan's Sword & Shield years, with an S-P suffix. The era began on 29 November 2019 with the V Starter Sets. Many came in Pokémon Card Gym Promo Card Packs; others came from campaigns, among them tie-ins with Pokémon GO, Champion's League and the Japan Championships, Extra Battle Day packs, Event Organizer Trainer's Packs, Pokémon Card Station classrooms, boxes, sets and starter decks, CoroCoro Comic, the Pokémon Center and Lawson.

description.text:
Cramorant came in Japan Post's Pokémon Stamp Box (ポケモン切手BOX～ポケモンカードゲーム 見返り美人・月に雁セット～), on sale from 25 August 2021, sealed in plastic with its partner card, Pikachu 227/S-P. Mitsuhiro Arita painted three Cramorant diving past a full moon in place of the wild geese of Utagawa Hiroshige's woodblock print Wild Geese Flying under the Full Moon (月に雁, about 1833), whose design became a Philatelic Week stamp in 1949. The box's sheet of stamps has a 120-yen stamp of the same picture.

Japan Post planned 80,000 boxes, then added 20,000 after a response beyond its expectations and sold every one by lottery; winners bought theirs at a post office, some not until late October. The card's attack, さんれんづき, flips three coins and does 60 damage for each heads.

description.text:
Pikachu came in Japan Post's Pokémon Stamp Box (ポケモン切手BOX～ポケモンカードゲーム 見返り美人・月に雁セット～), on sale from 25 August 2021, sealed in plastic with its partner card, Cramorant 226/S-P. Mitsuhiro Arita painted it perched on the shoulder of the woman in Hishikawa Moronobu's 17th-century painting Beauty Looking Back (見返り美人図), which in 1948 became the design of a Philatelic Week stamp so famous that its name stands for Japanese commemorative stamps. The box's sheet of stamps has a 120-yen stamp of the same picture.

Japan Post planned 80,000 boxes, then added 20,000 after a response beyond its expectations and sold every one by lottery; winners bought theirs at a post office, some not until late October. The card's one attack, いれかわる, switches Pikachu with one of your Benched Pokémon.

description.text: Victory Proof was the trophy card of Japan's Champions League in the Sword & Shield era, awarded at the 2020, 2021 and 2023 tournaments. It was never sold or given to entrants: only the top finishers of each league received one, in a print for their place. This 3rd Place print, from Champions League 2020 Aichi, went to the players who finished third and fourth in each league.
